title: Chicken Manchow Soup
description: Chicken Manchow Soup is a bold Indo-Chinese restaurant-style soup combining tender chicken, finely chopped vegetables, aromatic garlic, ginger, green chilies, soy sauce, and chili sauce in a rich chicken broth. Lightly thickened for a silky texture and finished with crispy fried noodles, garlic, and chicken, it delivers a satisfying contrast of heat, crunch, and savory depth.

ingredients.title: For the Soup Base
items: Bell peppers – ½ cup, finely chopped
Spring onions – 3–4, white and green parts separated
Cooked chicken – 1 cup, shredded or finely diced

ingredients.title: For Crispy Garlic & Chicken Garnish
items: Chicken breast – 2–3 small pieces, lightly fried or sautéed

ingredients.title: For the Fried Noodle Garnish
items: Thin crispy fried noodles – ½ cup

instruction.title: Step 1 – Preparing the Vegetables & Chicken
steps: Finely chop and slice all vegetables into small, uniform pieces.
Shred or finely dice the cooked chicken so it distributes evenly throughout the soup.
Separate the white and green portions of the spring onions.

instruction.title: Step 2 – Building the Soup Base
steps: Heat 1–2 tbsp oil in a wok over medium-high heat.
Add garlic, ginger, green chilies, and the white parts of the spring onions.
Sauté until fragrant without allowing the garlic to brown.
Add the chopped onion and cook until translucent.
Add carrots, cabbage, bell peppers, and mushrooms.
Stir-fry for 2–3 minutes while keeping the vegetables slightly crisp.
Add the cooked chicken and toss for approximately 1 minute to combine the flavors.

instruction.title: Step 3 – Adding the Chicken Broth
steps: Pour the chicken stock into the wok.
Add soy sauce, chili sauce, black pepper, and salt.
Bring the soup to a gentle boil and allow the flavors to meld.

instruction.title: Step 4 – Thickening the Soup
steps: Mix the cornstarch with 2 tbsp cold water until completely smooth.
Slowly pour the slurry into the boiling soup while stirring continuously.
Cook for 2–3 minutes until the soup becomes lightly thickened but remains pourable.

instruction.title: Step 5 – Preparing Crispy Garnishes
steps: Heat 1 tbsp oil in a small pan over medium heat.
Add the sliced garlic and fry until evenly golden and crisp.
Remove the garlic immediately and drain to prevent burning.
Lightly pan-fry the small chicken pieces until golden on the outside for an optional crunchy garnish.

instruction.title: Step 6 – Finishing the Soup
steps: Stir the green parts of the spring onions into the hot soup.
Taste and adjust the soy sauce, chili sauce, salt, or black pepper as needed.
Keep the soup hot until ready to plate.

instruction.title: Step 7 – Restaurant-Style Plating
steps: Use a wide, shallow white ceramic bowl to showcase the colors of the soup and garnishes.
Ladle the hot soup into the bowl.
Arrange shredded or pan-fried chicken neatly in the center.
Sprinkle crispy fried noodles over the top.
Scatter fried garlic slices and a few spring onion greens strategically around the garnish.
Add a few finely chopped red bell peppers or a tiny drizzle of chili oil for visual contrast if desired.
Finish with freshly cracked black pepper or a few drops of sesame oil for aroma.
Serve immediately while hot, optionally accompanied by a small bowl of chili sauce.

servingSuggestions.title: Serving Suggestions
items: Serve immediately as a hot Indo-Chinese appetizer.
Top with crispy fried noodles just before serving to preserve their crunch.
Pair with chicken fried rice, Hakka noodles, chili chicken, or other Indo-Chinese dishes.
Offer additional chili sauce or chili oil on the side for guests who prefer extra heat.

chefTips: Keep the vegetables slightly crunchy rather than fully soft for the characteristic Manchow Soup texture.
Use homemade chicken stock whenever possible for greater depth and richness.
Build the flavor in layers by sautéing garlic, ginger, chilies, and spring onion whites before adding the vegetables.
Add the cornstarch slurry gradually so the soup remains silky and pourable instead of becoming overly thick.
Fry garlic carefully and remove it as soon as it turns golden, as it can burn quickly.
Keep crispy noodles separate until plating so they retain maximum crunch.
For a spicier restaurant-style version, replace or supplement the chili sauce with Schezwan sauce.
For professional presentation, use a wide white bowl and arrange the chicken and garnishes centrally rather than scattering them randomly.
